architecture.ai_summary:
Liza turns a human goal into reviewed artifacts and integrated code. Language models make the judgments, and a Go binary enforces the rules. `liza init` binds a committed spec to a project-local YAML blackboard, the shared coordination file under .liza/, and to a declarative pipeline. The chosen entry point decides which stages still run: specification, architecture, planning, coding, and integration. An orchestrator breaks the goal into tasks and dependencies. Doer/reviewer role pairs produce and judge each artifact. Each agent runs under its own supervisor loop. The supervisor claims eligible work under lock before it launches a provider session (ADR-0006), prepares an isolated git worktree and a task-specific prompt, then processes the submission, verdict, and merge. Later stages receive structured task outputs and Git-anchored references, not conversation memory. Agents never talk to each other; they read state, work, and write state (ADR-0003). [README.md](README.md) explains the modes and philosophy, and [REPOSITORY.md](REPOSITORY.md) maps the docs. Use the purpose and hints fields and `stacklit derive` for navigation. This summary adds sequencing, authority boundaries, and what must change together.

The central boundary separates judgment from legality. Agents decide what satisfies a task; Go code decides which operations are allowed. Agents act only through CLI commands, many with --json envelopes. [ADR-0057](specs/architecture/ADR/0057-mcp-server-removal-cli-native-access-control.md) removed the MCP server described in ADR-0012 in favor of CLI-native access control, so treat older docs that mention liza-mcp as historical. Canonical lifecycle mutations use locked read-modify-write in internal/db/blackboard.go. Heartbeats publish generation-scoped records without the state lock; database reads overlay them and Modify folds them into state.yaml (ADR-0177). Hygiene validation runs before the state is published. That validation protects persistence; it does not replace domain checks. internal/ops/agent_authority.go rejects callers whose registration generation no longer matches the state, returning STALE_CALLER, so a replaced process cannot write over its successor. Provider launches and git work happen outside the blackboard transaction. A per-agent lifecycle lock is taken before the blackboard lock, so no provider side effect runs inside a state mutation. Ownership is lease-first. A heartbeat proves only that the supervisor is alive. A separate execution-progress watchdog watches task state, worktree changes, and provider output, and blocks stalled runs. Doer recovery order is handoff resume, then already-owned executing work, then fresh claims. [supervision-model.md](specs/architecture/supervision-model.md) is the authoritative recovery contract.

Review and merge are anchored to commits. internal/ops/submit_review.go requires ownership, executing status, a pre-execution checkpoint, and a submitted commit equal to the worktree HEAD. It then rebases onto the integration branch and validates review carriers and acceptance inputs. Its TDD gate (ADR-0007) only checks that test files changed or that a waiver was recorded. Whether the tests encode the intent remains the reviewer's judgment. internal/ops/wt_merge.go validates protected artifact references against the candidate tree, builds the merge commit without checking out integration, and advances the ref with a compare-and-swap via git update-ref. If integration tests fail, it rolls back only when the ref still points at its own merge, so concurrent merges are preserved, and the task becomes INTEGRATION_FAILED. A missing integration script only logs a warning, so a successful merge does not prove tests ran. [INVARIANTS.md](INVARIANTS.md) maps each invariant to its enforcing code and spec. Use its protection matrix (required by GUARDRAILS G1.2) before touching state, concurrency, review flow, agent lifecycle, or integration.

What must change together: a new lifecycle state or role touches pipeline transitions, claim eligibility, statevalidate rules, prompt context sections, allowed operations, and the TUI. A new provider capability spans the provider catalog, activation assets, launch resolution, and identity handling. Launch resolution lets an explicit CLI win over the profile CLI, which wins over role and global defaults (internal/agent/launch_resolver.go). Wording or rendering changes stay local when the operation contract is unchanged. Contract and skill text is mastered in contracts/ and skills/. make sync-embedded copies it into the binary, and builds and tests depend on that step. Config files and hooks are mastered directly in internal/embedded/. Optional Stacklit, SCIP, Semble, and functional-cluster indexes help navigation only, never verification. [architectural-issues.md](specs/architecture/architectural-issues.md) lists known coupling risks; check its dated entries against current code. The [ADR index](specs/architecture/ADR/README.md) gives rationale across about 165 decisions, and later ADRs often amend or supersede earlier ones.

Project-level constraints: go.mod targets Go 1.25.5. [GETTING_STARTED.md](GETTING_STARTED.md) supports Linux and macOS, plus experimental native Windows that requires Git Bash and excludes WSL, so process, path, and shell handling must stay platform-aware. [GUARDRAILS.md](GUARDRAILS.md) is binding. G1.1 requires runtime behavior to stay stack-agnostic: target-project commands must come from configuration or detection, never from this repository's Go tooling. G1.3 requires all presentation to go through internal/brand and rendered assets. The LIZA_* names in the hints are the default-brand spellings; a branded build can use its own prefix. G2.2 treats tokens in contracts, skills, and prompt templates as a shared budget, and internal/prompts/rolebudget enforces it. The license is Apache 2.0.
